summary: Boris Ivanovich Klyuev was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Moscow State University (~1947–1952, ~1960–1964). He held posts at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (1952–1971), CPSU Central Committee (1971–1982), MGIMO (1982–1988), and the Institute of Oriental Studies (1988).

Boris Ivanovich Pankratov studied at the Eastern Institute (~1912–1916). Specializing in Sinology, Tibetology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, he held positions at Far Eastern Federal University (1916), Harvard-Yenching Institute (1929–1935), the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts (1935–1942), Saint Petersburg State University (~1948–1972), and the University of Chicago (1948–1979).

Boris Karpushkin worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the Moscow Institute of Oriental Studies (~1946–1951) and later held positions at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences (1961–1974) and the Moscow State Institute of International Relations (1974).

Boris Leonidovič Smirnov worked in Indology and studied at the S. M. Kirov Military Medical Academy (~1909–1914). He served as Director of Turkmen State Medical University (~1939–1956) and as a Member of the Academy of Sciences of Turkmenistan (~1951–1967).

Boris Mikhailovich Lyapunov was a linguist who studied at Saint Petersburg State University (~1880–1885) under Vatroslav Jagić and Filipp Fedorovich Fortunatov. He held posts at the University of Kharkiv (1897–1899), Odesa University (1899–1923), and Saint Petersburg State University (1924).

Boris Stavisky specialized in history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies, studying at Saint Petersburg State University and the Saint Petersburg State Institute of History. He held posts at the Hermitage, State Museum of Oriental Art, Kara-Tepe Archaeological Expedition, All-Russian Scientific Research Institute for Restoration, and Moscow State University.

Boris Turayev worked in history and archaeology. He studied at the Faculty of History and Philology of St. Petersburg University (~1887–1891) and under Adolf Erman (~1894–1896), later holding a post at Saint Petersburg State University / Imperial St. Petersburg University (~1896–1920).

Boris Vladimirovich Semichov was a scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies who studied under Theodore Stcherbatsky (~1925–1929). He held a post at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts of the Russian Academy of Sciences (~1929–1937).

Boris Vladimirovič Semičëv studied at Saint Petersburg State University (~1923–1929) under Fyodor Shcherbatskoy. Working in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies, he held posts at the Institute of Buddhist Culture (1928–1932), University of Chicago (1930–1933), Peter the Great Museum of Anthropology and Ethnography (1932–1933), and Buryat Institute of Social Sciences (1955).

Boris Vladimirtsov studied at Saint Petersburg State University (~1904–1909) and under Antoine Meillet and Paul Pelliot (~1911–1912). Working in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Tibetology, he held posts at Saint Petersburg State University (1915), the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts (~1918–1931), and the National Library of Russia (1924–1925).

Boris Vsevolodovič Miller, an Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics scholar, studied at Moscow State University and the Lazarev Institute of Oriental Languages. He held posts at the State Russian Museum, National Museum of Tatarstan, State Museum of Ethnology, Institute of Linguistics, University of Chicago, Military Academy of Turin, and Moscow State University.
Bortolo Maria Bortolazzi was an Indology scholar who taught Greek at the Ginnasio Comunale di Bassano (1853–1854) and held a post at the Liceo Classico Jacopo Stellini until 1860.
Botrul Dongak Tenpai Nyima was a scholar in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied at Śrī Siṃha Shedra under Tubten Nyendrak, Khenpo Genam, and Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang.

Boyd Michailovsky is a linguist and Tibetologist who earned his Ph.D. at the University of California (-1981). He was affiliated with UC Berkeley (attested 1976–1978), the CNRS as Directeur de recherche (1979–2010), and Langues et Civilisations à Tradition Orale (attested 1990).
Bożena Śliwczyńska is an Indologist who studied under Maria Byrski. She is attested as a faculty member at the University of Warsaw in 2026.

Bradford Lyman Phillips studied Buddhist studies and Tibetology at Naropa University, Harvard University (M.T.S. -1993), and the University of Virginia (B.A. -1989; PhD -2004). His teachers and advisors included David Germano, Cecil Y. Lang, Michael Aris, Masatoshi Nagatomi, and Jeffrey Hopkins.
Bradley L. Herling is a scholar in religious studies and philosophy. He held posts as Assistant Director at Boston University and at Marymount Manhattan College (attested 2008).

Braj Basi Lal worked in archaeology and Indology, studying at the University of Allahabad (~1941–1943) and under Mortimer Wheeler (1943). He was Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India (1968–1972), department head at Jiwaji University (1970–1975), and Director of the Indian Institute of Advanced Study (1976–1986).

Brandon Dotson, a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology, completed his DPhil at the University of Oxford under Charles Ramble (~2002–2006) and his habilitation at the University of Munich (~2009–2013). He held posts at the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences (2002), SOAS (~2006–2010), and the University of Munich (~2010–2017).

Brandon J. Harwood works in philosophy and religious studies. He studied under Patrick Pranke at the University of Louisville, receiving a PhD attested in 2015, and held a post there in 2018 as Project Coordinator and Senior Lecturer.
